A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MISTR/MISTR-IV research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices A–C are available and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Sections 6–8 report original simulations, MIMIC-IV semi-simulations, and analyses of ACTG 175 HIV and Illinois unemployment data. The appendices include additional results and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experimental and data-analysis results in Sections 6–8 and the appendices, including numerical comparisons and sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: Sections 4–5 and Algorithm 1 retain the same recursive imputation, causal-forest estimation, aggregation and instrumental-variable extension. No algorithmic component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic censoring and instrumental-variable scenarios, MIMIC-IV semi-simulations, ACTG 175 analyses and Illinois unemployment experiments, including all appendix scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged, including CSF, T-learner and X-learner in Table S3 and IPCW-IV in the IV comparisons. The repaired random-survival-forest citations in Section 6.1 concern results attributed to prior work, not newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Sampling distributions, training and test sizes, MIMIC folds, forest configurations, survival horizons and evaluation metrics remain unchanged in Sections 6–8 and the experimental appendices.

E4.justification: The weak-instrument experiments in Section 6.3, additional-censoring HIV analysis, and bag-size and imputation-count sensitivity analyses in Appendix B are retained without revisions.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same uncertainty reporting and replication counts: 100 for synthetic/IV experiments, five for MIMIC, ten for HIV analyses and 50 for imputation-count sensitivity. Variance-estimation procedures are unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical entries and plotted findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 2 retains MIMIC-1 MSE values of 8.741 for CSF and 6.262 for MISTR, both scaled by 100.

T1.justification: Equations and assumptions are unchanged. Section 3 adds that h is a constant, clarifying the horizon already specified by Assumption A.1 rather than introducing a new definition or assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion retain the same claims about MISTR's performance under heavy censoring and MISTR-IV's applicability and novelty.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and result interpretations are unchanged. Both versions retain the complier-effect qualification in Section 5 and the ground-truth and domain-interpretation limitations discussed in Section 8.

D1.justification: Implementation settings in Appendix A, technical details in Appendices B–C, and the Data and Code Availability statement are unchanged. No new implementation or resource-access information is supplied.

R1.justification: Section 6.1 replaces two unresolved citations with Ishwaran and Kogalur (2019) for random survival forests and Lu et al. (2018) for enriched random survival forests. Both bibliography entries are added; the surrounding research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 corrects a missing 'in' in the introduction and 'make us' to 'make use' in Section 4, repairs citation punctuation, clarifies that h is constant, and updates dates. Section organization and the broader narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added references reflow the bibliography across pages 19–21, and corrected passages have limited line-wrapping changes. All figures and tables retain their content, captions, placement and design.

improvement.justification: Repairing the two unresolved citations in Section 6.1 improves attribution, while the wording corrections and horizon clarification improve readability. The scientific content and appendix evidence are unchanged, making this a limited editorial improvement.
